subject.title: [Bug]: Rejected oversized fork retires parent Codex binding

question: Should a focused repair proceed from the deterministic persisted-state evidence, or must the failure first be reproduced on current main with a real Codex app-server session?
rationale: The report strongly isolates a destructive state mutation, but the issue is explicitly routed for live reproduction and direct confirmation of the current-main hook order before changing a compatibility-sensitive session lifecycle.

options.title: Reproduce, then repair
options.body: Run an oversized fork against current main, capture the binding row before and after rejection, and proceed with the focused ordering fix if the parent is retired.

options.title: Repair from source evidence
options.body: Accept the deterministic report and source-level ordering proof as sufficient to implement the narrow validation-before-mutation fix without waiting for another live session.

recommendation.title: Reproduce, then repair
recommendation.body: Run an oversized fork against current main, capture the binding row before and after rejection, and proceed with the focused ordering fix if the parent is retired.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest available routing candidate for deciding whether the current evidence is sufficient for a sensitive Codex session-lifecycle repair.
